title: the DSG structural decay

banner.title: The DSG STRUCTURAL DECAY, R516: printed p. 43 (pdf 44) - the underground environment inflicting relatively swift decay upon wooden structures, the typical-location assumption of very humid air, the almost-completely-dry areas where wooden objects decay at a mere 2 or 3% of the given rate, the 1d6-year rot onset for anything made of wood and kept underground, the creosote-or-sealant doubling of the onset period, the 5% chance of collapse per multiple of the onset roll that passes with the roll-1 structure at 5% per year and a 20-year maximum (100%) and the roll-6 structure lasting as much as 120 years, the check whenever any activity puts unusual stress upon the structure, and the d100 roll against the percentage chance of collapse
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~5500-5525) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 62 = printed p. 43) - every number dual-confirmed: the 2 or 3% dry band, the 1d6-year rot onset (the djvu garble 146 = 1d6 settled by the Capture read), the creosote doubling, the 5%-per-multiple collapse chance with the roll-1 = 20-year and roll-6 = 120-year worked examples, and the stress check made with a d100 roll (the djvu garble 4100 = d100). The Underground Waterways section starts the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: No table in this section - the pins are consts and bools only. The 1d6 rot onset pins as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention. The collapse math stays prose: the 20-year and 120-year worked examples pin as consts but the engine multiplies nothing - nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnsDryRateLowPct
consts.comment: in subterranean areas that are almost completely dry, the decay of wooden objects is a mere 2 or 3% of the rate given.

consts.name: dnsDryRateHighPct
consts.comment: the high end of the almost-completely-dry decay band: a mere 2 or 3% of the typical humid rate (the djvu garble class: 2 or 3% reads clean).

consts.name: dnsRotOnsetYearsDice
consts.comment: anything made out of wood and kept underground begins to show signs of rot after 1d6 years - the dice of the onset roll (the djvu garble 146 = 1d6, settled by the Capture read).

consts.name: dnsRotOnsetYearsSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d6-year rot-onset roll, pinned as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention.

consts.name: dnsCreosotePeriodMultiplier
consts.comment: if the wood is soaked in creosote or some other sealing substance, this period is doubled.

consts.name: dnsCollapseChancePerMultiplePct
consts.comment: the rot creates a 5% chance of collapse for each multiple of the 1d6 onset roll that passes.

consts.name: dnsRollOneMaxYears
consts.comment: if the first roll was a 1, there is a 5% chance of collapse every year, and the structure would last a maximum of 20 years (at which time the chance of collapse is 100%).

consts.name: dnsRollSixMaxYears
consts.comment: if the original roll was a 6, however, the structure might last as much as 120 years (6 multiples x the 5% ladder).

bools.name: dnsHumidAirAssumed
bools.comment: the underground environment inflicts relatively swift decay upon wooden structures; the effects assume the presence of very humid air, the typical underground location.

bools.name: dnsDryAreasMereFractionOfRate
bools.comment: in almost completely dry subterranean areas the wooden decay runs at a mere 2 or 3% of the given rate.

bools.name: dnsCreosoteOrSealantDoubles
bools.comment: creosote or some other sealing substance doubles the rot-onset period.

bools.name: dnsCollapseChancePerMultipleOfOnset
bools.comment: the collapse chance accrues per multiple of the 1d6 onset roll that passes - the roll sets both the interval and the lifetime.

bools.name: dnsCheckOnUnusualStress
bools.comment: the wooden structure should be checked whenever any activity puts unusual stress upon it.

bools.name: dnsStressCheckIsD100
bools.comment: the check is made with a d100 roll (the djvu garble 4100 = d100, settled by the Capture read) against the percentage chance of collapse for the structure.

examples.note: the dry-area band: almost completely dry areas decay at a mere 2 or 3% of the typical humid rate.
the rot onset: wooden things underground show rot after 1d6 years, doubled to 2d6 by creosote or another sealing substance (the djvu garble 146 = 1d6).
the collapse ladder: 5% per multiple of the onset roll - the roll-1 structure reaches 100% at 20 years, the roll-6 structure might last 120 years.
